cast.theme: Weekly meeting of a university ecology research lab

personas.name: Elena
personas.goals: A productive season and June graduating on time
personas.hidden_agenda: The grant renewal depends on this season's data

personas.name: June
personas.hidden_agenda: Behind on processing and embarrassed about it

personas.name: Felix
personas.goals: Keep the equipment alive and the budget sane
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been fixing camera traps on weekends

pack.title: Hollis Lab weekly meeting
pack.org: Hollis Lab, Department of Ecology, Northfield University (fictional)

agenda.title: Data and sample backlog
agenda.goal: Get an honest status on processing and what to sequence

agenda.title: Papers and deadlines
agenda.goal: Agree priorities between the thesis chapter and the side paper

agenda.title: Lab operations and budget
agenda.goal: Check the grant balance and the lab's practical needs

beats.summary: Dates, sites and traps; Tariq gets the permit date wrong and nobody notices
The backlog is bigger than June says; deciding what to sequence
Thesis chapter vs the side paper; Elena misremembers the abstract deadline, June corrects her
The grant balance and a quiet fight about the freezer

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Right, let's start. Field season first, since it's coming up fast. Tariq?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Basically, we're on track for May eighteenth, all fourteen sites.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: All fourteen, including the ridge sites?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Including the ridge. The access road was cleared last week.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: For what it's worth, the camera traps are the bottleneck. Thirty-six of the forty work.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: What's wrong with the other four?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: Two have dead boards, two have cracked housings. The housings I can fix. The boards, not really.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Do we need all forty out at once?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: In the field we lose a few to bears every season, so yes, basically.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: I'll order two replacement boards this week, out of the equipment line.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Thank you, Felix.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: And the permit is good through the end of May, so no rush there.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Good. One less thing.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Are the undergrads confirmed?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Five confirmed. One more maybe, if her summer class gets cancelled.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Five is enough. A sixth would be nice.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Somebody needs to do the safety training with them before we go.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Has anyone heard back from the parks office about site nine?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: Sorry, the truck. We should talk about the truck.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Right, the truck rental is five forty a week. For the whole season that adds up.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: We could share with the Okafor lab, they're out at the same time.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Maybe we split the truck with Okafor. Let me think about it.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: In the field, sharing a truck means somebody's always waiting.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Okay, the season starts May eighteenth, all fourteen sites. That's locked.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Locked. Finally.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Data. June, where are we with processing?

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: I think, um, we've processed about twelve hundred.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And what's left?

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: About two hundred? Maybe a bit more.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: For what it's worth, the freezer log says three hundred and eighty still unprocessed.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Sorry. Yes. I was counting the ones I'd already sorted. It's three eighty.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That's okay. It's better to know now. How long would three eighty take you?

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Honestly, at my current pace, most of the summer.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Which is exactly when you need to be writing.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Right. Let's be strategic. Do we need to sequence all of them?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Basically, no. Half of them are the replicate sites. The core sites matter more.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: Sequencing is eighteen dollars a sample, so three eighty is real money anyway.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: If we only did the core sites, I think it's about half of them.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Then we sequence the core-site samples first and leave the replicates for the fall. That's the plan.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Okay. That's, okay, that's a relief, actually.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: I can help with sorting if I'm not in the field.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Tariq, you're going to be in the field.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Right, true.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: I'll set up a shared sheet so we can see what's left, site by site.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Did anyone else see the bear video from the ridge camera?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: The one where it licks the lens? I've watched it about ten times.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: My mom made it her phone background.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Okay, that's very good, and we're moving on. Deadlines. The conference abstract is due February twelfth, if I remember right.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Sorry, I think it's the second. February second.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The second. That's, okay, that's sooner.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: And the revision for the moth paper is due March ninth.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Do I have to be on the moth paper revision?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: You're second author. But the chapter matters more.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: The reviewers mostly want the stats redone. Basically, that's me anyway.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Then let's be strategic. June, the chapter comes first, the moth revision is Tariq's. Settled.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Thank you. Really.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: I'll redo the stats for the moth revision by the end of February.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And the abstract? Who's writing it?

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: It should probably come from the chapter data.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Maybe. If the chapter goes okay. I don't know.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Let's see where the chapter is next week before we commit to the abstract.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Is it okay if I skip the reading group until the chapter's done?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: For a few weeks, yes.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Okay. Great.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Last thing, lab ops. Felix, the money.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: Remaining on the grant is twenty-seven four.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: That's less than I thought.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: The sequencing and the truck are the big ones this summer.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: Sorry, someone's knocking, it's the department admin with a package.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: No worries.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Is the minus-eighty freezer still making that noise?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: It is. For what it's worth, I think the compressor's going.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: If that freezer dies, we lose everything June hasn't processed.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Please don't say that.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Should we move the samples to the department freezer as a backup?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: The department freezer is full. I asked last month.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Could we get the compressor serviced before the season?

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: Probably. It's a few hundred dollars, not thousands.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Then let's get it serviced. Out of this year's money. Done.

turns.speaker: Felix
turns.text: I'll call the service company tomorrow and book it.

turns.speaker: Tariq
turns.text: What happens to the samples while it's being serviced?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Right, I think that's everything. Good meeting. June, chapter.

turns.speaker: June
turns.text: Chapter. Got it.
